diveTitle: What actually happens when you convert
diveSubtitle: When WebP saves space, and when it doesn't.
dive1Title: Lossy vs. lossless WebP — which do we use?
dive1Desc: WebP supports both modes. We convert PNG using lossless WebP compression by default, since PNG itself is lossless — this keeps every pixel identical while still shrinking the file, rather than introducing quality loss you didn't ask for.
dive2Desc: WebP fully supports transparency, just like PNG, so any transparent areas in your source image carry over exactly. This is one of WebP's real advantages over JPG, which can't represent transparency at all.
dive3Title: How much smaller does the file actually get?
dive3Desc: Lossless WebP typically produces files 25-35% smaller than the equivalent PNG with identical visual quality — the exact savings depend on the image's content, with detailed photos compressing less than flat-color graphics.
dive4Title: Browser and app support for WebP
dive4Desc: All modern browsers — Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge — support WebP natively, and most image editors and CMS platforms accept it too. Older software or some email clients may not display WebP — if compatibility is uncertain, keep the PNG as a fallback.
dive5Desc: This tool is built for static PNG images. An animated PNG converts using only its first frame, since WebP's own animation format works differently — a dedicated APNG-to-animated-WebP tool handles that conversion if you need an animated result.
dive6Desc: WebP to PNG conversion is lossless in the reverse direction too, when the WebP was created losslessly in the first place — you'll get the original pixel data back. If the WebP was created with lossy compression, that quality loss can't be recovered by converting back.
faqSubtitle: Quick answers on limits, privacy and results.
faq1Question: Is the PNG to WEBP converter free?
faq1Answer: Yes — you can use it for free, without creating an account and without watermarks. The free plan allows 5 uses per day and has a file-size limit; paid plans raise them.
faq2Question: Will converting to WEBP reduce image quality?
faq2Answer: No. Our converter uses lossless WEBP encoding, which preserves every pixel. You get a smaller file with identical visual quality.
faq3Question: Does WEBP support transparency like PNG?
faq3Answer: Yes. WEBP fully supports alpha transparency, so your transparent PNGs will remain transparent after conversion.
faq4Question: How much smaller will my files be?
faq4Answer: Typically 25–35% smaller than the original PNG. The exact reduction depends on image content, but WEBP consistently outperforms PNG in file size.
faq5Question: Is WEBP supported by all browsers?
faq5Answer: Yes. WEBP is supported by Chrome, Firefox, Safari (since 14), Edge, and all modern mobile browsers. It is now the standard format for web images.
seoSection1Title: What Is WEBP and Why Should You Use It?
seoSection1Para1: WEBP is a modern image format developed by Google, designed specifically for the web. It uses advanced compression algorithms to deliver smaller file sizes than PNG and JPEG while maintaining excellent visual quality.
seoSection1Para2: For website owners, switching from PNG to WEBP can significantly improve page load speed, reduce bandwidth usage, and boost Core Web Vitals scores — all factors that affect SEO rankings.
seoSection2Para: PNG is a lossless format ideal for graphics with transparency, while WEBP compresses further. A PNG logo that weighs 150 KB can often be reduced to under 100 KB as WEBP, with no visible quality difference.
seoSection3Title: When to Use WEBP on Your Website
seoSection3Para: Use WEBP for all images on your website — product photos, blog images, icons, and logos. Most modern CMS platforms like WordPress, Shopify, and Webflow support WEBP natively. Converting your existing PNG library to WEBP is one of the easiest performance wins available.
